title: Factory extraction: ticks becomes terminal-first, the factory becomes ticfac
description:
PROJECT container. Spec: docs/projects/2026-08-27-factory-extraction/2026-08-27-factory-extraction-spec.md — read it first; every epic below is a phase of it.

THE DECISION (Peter, 2026-08-27): ticks is a product for a user at a terminal, optimised for the longest autonomous runs possible. The cloud factory is a separate product that USES ticks. Today the factory is ~56k lines of TypeScript, ~13k of Go, 13 applied D1 migrations and 21 of tk's 84 subcommands living inside ticks, and its own design doc still says "nothing here is implemented".

THREE CALLS MADE WHILE SCOPING, recorded here so they are not relitigated per-epic:

1. THE OPERATOR PACKAGE SPLITS. `internal/operator` is two things under one name. The durable question store (2,636 lines) STAYS — herd_wait.go:209 parks a blocked agent's question "for terminal answer with tk answer" when no channel is configured, and that is precisely what a long autonomous run at a terminal needs. The Telegram transport (3,064 lines) GOES.

2. THE TELEGRAM DUPLICATION IS RESOLVED BY RETIREMENT, NOT RELOCATION. One bot token has exactly one reader: the Go side long-polls getUpdates (a second gets 409), the Worker registers a webhook, and the two are mutually exclusive. The webhook wins — it is deployed, a poller needs a laptop that stays awake (the exact failure the factory exists to remove), and the Worker's module doc already declares the front door. tk channel and tk tell keep their names and become factory-API clients. A bot token stops living on laptops.

3. THE NEW REPO IS PUBLIC, with ticks' public-repo guard copied over. The code is public today; flipping to private is always available and the reverse is not. The factory's own design says it ships the blueprint, not the plant — operator-specific values already live in ~/.ticksrc and the operator's own Cloudflare account, never in the tree.

TWO REMAINING OPEN QUESTIONS, deliberately not answered here — they belong to the epics that hit them: whether the sandbox IMAGE (cloud/sandbox/*.sh) follows the factory while internal/sandbox Go stays (the Go tests execute those scripts), and whether `cloud` survives as a substrate NAME in .tick/runners.toml after the implementation leaves.

SHAPE OF THE RUN: phases 0-4b are entirely inside this repo and each is independently valuable even if the extraction is abandoned — that property is what makes it safe to start. Only phase 5 creates ticfac and moves anything.

INTEGRATION, per .tick/config.md: epic branches go through a PR + CI gate. No direct merges to the default branch. This differs from other repos this orchestrator has run.
